corrected_draft.description_long: Reuters Fact Check reported in September 2024 that viral allegations about Haitian immigrants in Springfield, Ohio, stealing and eating pets were unsupported. Springfield police said there were no credible reports or specific claims of pets being harmed by members of the immigrant community. City officials also said reports about geese or ducks taken from parks could not be verified. event_identity_comparison.original_title: They're Eating the Dogs: Springfield Ohio Haitian Pet-Eating Hoax Drives 2025 Immigration Crackdown
event_identity_comparison.original_summary: The Haitians are eating pets disinformation campaign — launched from a fourth-hand Facebook post in a local Springfield, Ohio crime group — was amplified into national policy by Trump and JD Vance, with consequences that continued to shape immigration enforcement throughout 2025. Vance posted the baseless claim on September 9, 2024 to 11.1 million views on X, and Trump repeated it on the debate stage on September 11, 2024 — They're eating the dogs. They're eating the cats. They're eating the pets of the people that live there — despite debate moderators immediately citing Springfield's own city manager confirming no credible reports existed. Springfield Mayor Rob Rue and police repeatedly confirmed there were no credible reports or specific claims of pets being harmed, injured or abused by individuals within the immigrant community, and the one animal-cruelty case cited had occurred 160 miles away in Canton and involved a non-Haitian Ohio resident. The campaign continued to drive policy in 2025: the Trump administration cut Haitian Temporary Protected Status short by six months, setting expiration for August 3, 2025 rather than the original December deadline, stripping legal protection from thousands of Haitians who had arrived through lawful humanitarian parole programs. PolitiFact documented that Vance had cherry-picked limited statistics to claim an 81% murder spike linked to Springfield's Haitian community — a figure that masked a longer-term crime decline — and White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt continued to characterize all humanitarian parolees as illegal immigrants, despite federal judges ruling the characterization legally false.
